title: They called them cockroaches, then the Cockroaches swarmed them
body: In May, India's Chief Justice Surya Kant called unemployed young people "like cockroaches" and "parasites of society" from the Supreme Court bench. They took the insult and put it on a banner. Within 78 hours a satirical Instagram page had three million followers. Al Jazeera reports it grew into the Cockroach Janta Party, a straight pun on Modi's ruling BJP.

For more than a month, hundreds of thousands filled Jantar Mantar in the heart of Delhi, with sit-ins and hunger strikes spreading to Pune, Bengaluru, and Lucknow. The anger started over leaked exam papers used to determine which jobs are given to who, then turned into something bigger about a government that had stopped listening. Dropsite reports that on Saturday Modi's government caved and accepted every demand. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan announced his resignation on X. NPR and NBC covered the same result.

A powerful man reached for a slur to make young people feel small. They turned it into a name, a party, and a minister out of a job. Call people anything long enough, and don't be shocked when they organize under the moniker.
